paper.place: The sharp bound before composition
paper.claim: For n ≥ 1, the nth Taylor coefficient of f at zero has modulus at most Aₙ(p) = (1−p²ⁿ)/((1−p²)pⁿ⁻¹). The bound is sharp at every degree.
paper.source_words: $a_n$ at the origin satisfy the sharp bound

paper.place: Taylor coefficients of the subordinate map
paper.claim: If h maps the disk holomorphically into itself and fixes zero, f∘h is holomorphic near zero even when it has poles elsewhere in the disk.
paper.source_words: poles, but it is holomorphic near $0$

paper.place: The unweighted bound in all degrees
paper.claim: For every n ≥ 1 and 0 < p < 1, the nth coefficient of f∘h has modulus at most Aₙ(p). Equality at n ≥ 2 requires both the extremal f(z) = z/((1−pz)(1−z/p)) and a rotation h.

paper.place: Two derivative conjectures of 2008
paper.claim: Theorem 3 gives the sharp bounds conjectured by Avkhadiev and Wirths in 2008 for derivatives of order n ≥ 2 at finite values of a meromorphic map. Its source is the disk or a proper convex plane domain, and its target is a simply connected spherical domain omitting at least two points.
paper.source_words: derivatives of a meromorphic map from the disk, or from a convex domain

paper.place: Three ingredients of the coefficient estimate
paper.claim: For each coefficient index the transfer lemma supplies a holomorphic disk weight bounded by one. The slit map fixes zero and has positive Taylor coefficients in positive degrees. Robertson’s inequality bounds the odd coefficients used in the product estimate.

paper.place: The disk of the Taylor expansion
paper.claim: Every f in M(p) is holomorphic on |z| < p, where its Taylor series has constant term zero and linear term z.
paper.source_words: $|z|<p$, so it has a Taylor expansion

paper.place: The coefficient estimate for M(p)
paper.claim: For f in M(p) and n ≥ 1, |[zⁿ]f| ≤ Aₙ(p), with equality attained by fₚ.

paper.place: Two expressions for the coefficient bound
paper.claim: For n ≥ 1 and 0 < p < 1, Aₙ(p) = p¹⁻ⁿ(1+p²+⋯+p²ⁿ⁻²) = (1−p²ⁿ)/((1−p²)pⁿ⁻¹).

paper.place: Uniqueness of the unweighted base extremal
paper.claim: For each n ≥ 2, a function f in M(p) attains |[zⁿ]f| = Aₙ(p) exactly when f = fₚ on the disk.

paper.place: Coefficients of the rational extremal
paper.claim: For every n ≥ 1, [zⁿ]fₚ = Aₙ(p). The same function attains all the base bounds.

paper.place: Poles and regularity of the composition
paper.claim: For f in M(p) and a Schwarz function h, f∘h is meromorphic on 𝔻 with poles exactly where h(z) = p. It is holomorphic on |z| < p.
paper.source_words: It has a pole at every point where $h$ takes the value $p$

paper.place: Loss of injectivity under subordination
paper.claim: Even for f in M(p), f∘h can fail to be injective. For instance, h ≡ 0 gives a constant composite.
paper.source_words: in general it is not one-to-one

paper.place: Conjecture 1 — the generalized Goodman bound
paper.claim: For every 0 < p < 1, every f in M(p), every Schwarz function h, and every n ≥ 1, |[zⁿ](f∘h)| ≤ Aₙ(p).

paper.place: Rogosinski’s holomorphic coefficient bound
paper.claim: For F in S, every Schwarz function h, and n ≥ 1, |[zⁿ](F∘h)| ≤ n.

paper.place: The limit as the pole approaches the circle
paper.claim: For each fixed n ≥ 1, Aₙ(p) tends to n as p increases to 1.

paper.place: Figure 1 — coverage of Theorem 1
paper.claim: The right panel represents the bound for all f in M(p), every 0 < p < 1, and every n ≥ 1, including the degrees beyond those displayed.

paper.place: Theorem 1 — coefficients with a bounded weight
paper.claim: For 0 < p < 1, f in M(p), h a Schwarz function, and e holomorphic on 𝔻 with |e| ≤ 1, the nth Taylor coefficient of e · (f∘h) has modulus at most Aₙ(p) for every n ≥ 1.

paper.place: Theorem 1 — equality in degree two and higher
paper.claim: For e ≡ 1 and each n ≥ 2, equality holds exactly when f = fₚ on 𝔻 and h(z) = λz for a constant λ with |λ| = 1.
paper.source_words: equality holds if and only if $f=f_p$ and $h(z)=\lambda z$

paper.place: Theorem 1 — equality in degree one
paper.claim: For e ≡ 1 and n = 1, every f in M(p) attains equality with precisely the Schwarz functions h(z) = λz, |λ| = 1.
paper.source_words: For $e=1$ and $n=1$, equality holds exactly when

paper.place: Normalization of hyperbolic distance
paper.claim: The conformal radius is independent of the centered chart. Hyperbolic distance has curvature −4 normalization, so δ_𝔻(0,r) = artanh r for 0 ≤ r < 1.
paper.source_words: normalized by curvature $-4$, so that $\delta_\D(0,r)=\artanh r$

paper.place: Theorem 2 — distance to infinity
paper.claim: When ∞ belongs to Π and w₀ = G(0) is finite, p = tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞) lies strictly between 0 and 1.

paper.place: Theorem 2 — derivatives at the disk origin
paper.claim: For a holomorphic map G from 𝔻 into a simply connected spherical domain Π containing ∞ and omitting at least two points, with G(0) = w₀ finite, |G⁽ⁿ⁾(0)|/n! ≤ R(w₀,Π) Aₙ(p) for every n ≥ 1, where p = tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞).

paper.place: Theorem 2 — geometric equality criterion
paper.claim: For each n ≥ 2, equality holds exactly when G maps 𝔻 conformally onto Π and the complement of Π is a line segment whose supporting line passes through w₀.
paper.source_words: a line segment lying on a line through $w_0$

paper.place: The endpoint coefficient bound for planar targets
paper.claim: At the planar endpoint p = 1, Aₖ(1) = k is the limit of Aₖ(p) as p increases to 1, for each k ≥ 1.

paper.place: Closed form for the derivative bound
paper.claim: For 0 < p < 1 and 0 ≤ r ≤ 1, Dₙ(p,r) = ((r+1/p)ⁿ⁻¹ − p²(r+p)ⁿ⁻¹)/(1−p²).

paper.place: Theorem 3(a) — derivatives at a disk point
paper.claim: For meromorphic G from 𝔻 into a simply connected spherical domain Π omitting at least two points, at every z₀ with finite G(z₀) and every n ≥ 2, Rₛⁿ |G⁽ⁿ⁾(z₀)|/(n! Rₜ) ≤ Dₙ(p,|z₀|), including p = 1.

paper.place: Theorem 3(b) — derivatives on a convex source
paper.claim: For meromorphic G from a proper convex plane domain into a simply connected spherical domain Π omitting at least two points, at every z₀ with finite G(z₀) and every n ≥ 2, Rₛⁿ |G⁽ⁿ⁾(z₀)|/(n! Rₜ) ≤ Dₙ(p,1), including p = 1.

paper.place: Theorem 3 — sharpness of both derivative bounds
paper.claim: Both bounds are attained for every 0 < p ≤ 1 and n ≥ 2. The extremal maps use fₚ, with the Koebe function f₁(z) = z/(1−z)² at p = 1.
paper.source_words: Both bounds are sharp for every $p$ and $n$

paper.place: Disk derivative bounds from earlier coefficient ranges
paper.claim: The disk change of center and the 2009 Theorem 8.3 already give Theorem 3(a) for n = 2 at all 0 < p < 1, for n = 3 at p < 0.7, and for n ≥ 4 at p < 1/(2n−2).

paper.place: Replacing composition by a bounded multiplier
paper.claim: For a fixed degree n, the nth coefficient of e · (f∘h) equals that of Ef for some holomorphic |E| ≤ 1. For e ≡ 1 the polynomial form occurs in Rogosinski’s work and in Szapiel’s later reduction.

paper.place: Removing the pole by a slit-disk chart
paper.claim: The conformal map q from 𝔻 ∖ [p,1) onto 𝔻 fixes zero and has positive coefficients in every positive degree. With slit-disk conformal radius R = 4p/(1+p)², the pullback (f∘q⁻¹)/R belongs to S.

paper.place: Summing the product bounds against the slit coefficients
paper.claim: Robertson’s inequality gives |[wᵏ](FE)| ≤ k for F in S and holomorphic |E| ≤ 1. Near zero, the resulting majorant R(q+2q²+3q³+⋯) equals fₚ.

paper.place: Recovering the base estimate from de Branges’s bound
paper.claim: With e ≡ 1 and h(z) = z, the slit representation and |[wᵏ]F| ≤ k for F in S give |[zⁿ]f| ≤ Aₙ(p) for f in M(p) and n ≥ 1.

paper.place: Lemma 4 — transfer of one coefficient for every germ
paper.claim: For a Schwarz function h, a holomorphic disk weight |e| ≤ 1, and each n ≥ 0, there exists a holomorphic disk weight |E| ≤ 1 that satisfies [zⁿ](e · (g∘h)) = [wⁿ](Eg) for every g holomorphic near zero, and E(0) = e(0)h′(0)ⁿ.

paper.place: Only the first n degrees of the germ contribute
paper.claim: Since h fixes zero, hʲ vanishes to order at least j. Terms of g above degree n contribute zero to [zⁿ](e · (g∘h)).

paper.place: The coefficient functional on polynomials
paper.claim: On polynomials, the linear functional Λ(P) = [zⁿ](e · (P∘h)) satisfies |Λ(P)| ≤ ∫ |P| dσ, where σ is normalized arc measure on the unit circle.

paper.place: The weighted coefficient as a finite sum
paper.claim: For g holomorphic near zero with coefficients gⱼ, [zⁿ](e · (g∘h)) is the sum of gⱼ Λ(wʲ) over j = 0,…,n.

paper.place: A harmonic majorant for the polynomial
paper.claim: The Poisson integral U of the boundary function |P| majorizes |P| on 𝔻, and U∘h is harmonic there.
paper.source_words: $|P|\le U$ in $\D$, and $U\circ h$ is harmonic

paper.place: Cauchy’s estimate on an interior circle
paper.claim: For 0 < r < 1, rⁿ |Λ(P)| is at most the normalized circle average of |P(h(rζ))|.

paper.place: The mean value of the harmonic majorant
paper.claim: For 0 < r < 1 the circle average of U(h(rζ)) equals U(0) = ∫ |P| dσ. Thus |Λ(P)| ≤ ∫ |P| dσ in the limit r ↑ 1.

paper.place: A bounded density representing the functional
paper.claim: There is a function v on the unit circle with essential supremum at most 1 such that Λ(P) = ∫ vP dσ for every polynomial P.

paper.place: Vanishing moments above the chosen degree
paper.claim: For every j > n, the moment Λ(wʲ) vanishes.

paper.place: Negative Fourier modes of the shifted density
paper.claim: For each m ≥ 1, the Fourier coefficient of wⁿv(w) at index −m is Λ(wⁿ⁺ᵐ) = 0.
paper.source_words: has no Fourier coefficients of negative index

paper.place: An analytic multiplier from boundary values
paper.claim: The function wⁿv(w) on the unit circle is the almost-everywhere boundary value of a holomorphic function E on 𝔻 with |E| ≤ 1.
paper.source_words: the boundary function of a holomorphic $E$ with $|E|\le1$

paper.place: Taylor coefficients of the multiplier as moments
paper.claim: For 0 ≤ j ≤ n, [wⁿ⁻ʲ]E = ∫ v(w)wʲ dσ(w) = Λ(wʲ).

paper.place: Reassembling the coefficient of the product
paper.claim: For every analytic germ g with coefficients gⱼ, the nth coefficient of Eg is the sum of gⱼ Λ(wʲ) over j = 0,…,n.

paper.place: The value of the transfer multiplier at zero
paper.claim: For every n ≥ 0 the representing multiplier satisfies E(0) = Λ(wⁿ) = e(0)h′(0)ⁿ.

paper.place: The unweighted transfer in degree zero
paper.claim: When e ≡ 1 and n = 0, the constant multiplier E ≡ 1 realizes the identity for every analytic germ g.

paper.place: The unweighted transfer polynomial
paper.claim: For e ≡ 1 and n ≥ 1, write cⱼ = [zⁿ]hʲ. The polynomial Q(w) = c₁wⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + cₙ satisfies [zⁿ](g∘h) = [wⁿ](Qg) for every g holomorphic near zero.

paper.place: Positive real part of the Cayley transform
paper.claim: For |t| = 1 the holomorphic function (1+th)/(1−th) has positive real part on 𝔻 and value 1 at zero.
paper.source_words: positive real part and value $1$ at the origin

paper.place: Coefficients of the Cayley transform
paper.claim: For n ≥ 1 and |t| = 1, the nth coefficient of (1+th)/(1−th) equals twice the sum of cⱼ tʲ over j = 1,…,n, where cⱼ = [zⁿ]hʲ.

paper.place: Carathéodory’s coefficient bound
paper.claim: For a holomorphic function on 𝔻 with positive real part and value 1 at zero, every positive-degree coefficient has modulus at most 2.

paper.place: The unit bound for the transfer polynomial
paper.claim: The unweighted transfer polynomial Q has |Q(w)| ≤ 1 on the unit circle and throughout the disk.

paper.place: Lemma 5 — the conformal slit map
paper.claim: For 0 < p < 1, let J(z) = z+1/z, B = p+1/p and R = 4/(B+2). A conformal bijection q from 𝔻 ∖ [p,1) onto 𝔻 fixes zero and satisfies J(q(z))+2 = R(J(z)+2) as a spherical identity.

paper.place: Lemma 5 — strict positivity in each positive degree
paper.claim: For every n ≥ 1, the Taylor coefficient [zⁿ]q is real and strictly positive.
paper.source_words: The coefficient of $z^n$ in $q$ is positive for every $n\ge1$

paper.place: Lemma 5 — the extremal as a convergent series
paper.claim: Near zero, R(q(z)+2q(z)²+3q(z)³+⋯) converges to fₚ(z).

paper.place: Figure 2 — the boundary arc traced by the slit
paper.claim: For p = 1/2, the two banks of the slit have boundary images on conjugate arcs meeting at 1. At the far ends of the arcs the real part tends to 7/9.
paper.source_words: the heavy arc of the unit circle around $1$

paper.place: Figure 2 — the role of positive slit coefficients
paper.claim: The positive-degree coefficients of q are positive, so its powers give nonnegative weights when the coefficient estimates of Lemma 6 are summed in Proposition 7.

paper.place: The Joukowski image of the unit disk
paper.claim: J(z) = z+1/z maps 𝔻 one-to-one onto the sphere minus [−2,2], sending zero to ∞. On [p,1) it decreases from B = p+1/p toward 2.

paper.place: Straightening the longer omitted interval
paper.claim: J maps the slit disk onto the sphere minus [−2,B]. The affine map x ↦ R(x+2)−2 fixes −2 and ∞ and sends B to 2, carrying this image onto the sphere minus [−2,2].
paper.source_words: $x\mapsto R(x+2)-2$ fixes $-2$ and $\infty$ and sends $B$ to $2$

paper.place: Construction of the centered slit chart
paper.claim: Conjugating x ↦ R(x+2)−2 by J gives q(z) = J⁻¹(R(J(z)+2)−2), with J⁻¹ taking values in 𝔻. The resulting conformal map fixes zero.
paper.source_words: the affine map fixes $\infty$, and $J^{-1}$ sends $\infty$ to $0$

paper.place: The slit-disk conformal radius
paper.claim: At zero, q′(0) = 1/R. Its inverse χ has χ′(0) = R, the conformal radius of 𝔻 ∖ [p,1) at zero.

paper.place: Factoring the equation for the slit map
paper.claim: The identity z(1+q)² = Rq(1+z)² gives (q−z)(1−zq) = cz(1+q)², where c = 1/R−1 = (1−p)²/(4p) > 0.

paper.place: A power-series recurrence for q
paper.claim: Near zero, q = z + cz(1+q)²(1+zq+(zq)²+⋯), with c = (1−p)²/(4p).

paper.place: The positive term in the coefficient recurrence
paper.claim: Writing qₙ = [zⁿ]q, one has q₁ = 1+c. For n ≥ 2, qₙ is a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients in c and the earlier qⱼ, containing the term 2c times the preceding coefficient.

paper.place: Rational form of the slit-map majorant
paper.claim: Near zero, Rq/(1−q)² = 1/(J(z)−B) = z/(1−Bz+z²) = fₚ(z), with the value at zero supplied by continuity.

paper.place: Lemma 6 — product with a bounded holomorphic factor
paper.claim: For F in S and E holomorphic on 𝔻 with |E| ≤ 1, |[wᵏ](FE)| ≤ k for every k ≥ 1.

paper.place: The normalized square root of F(w)/w
paper.claim: For F in S, the quotient F(w)/w extends holomorphically without zeros to 𝔻. It has a holomorphic square root M with M(0) = 1, so F(w) = wM(w)².

paper.place: The odd univalent function associated with F
paper.claim: The function F₂(z) = zM(z²) is odd and injective on 𝔻, has F₂′(0) = 1, and satisfies F₂(z)² = F(z²).

paper.place: Indexing the odd coefficients
paper.claim: For each j ≥ 0, the coefficient bⱼ = [wʲ]M equals [z²ʲ⁺¹]F₂. In particular b₀ = 1.

paper.place: Truncating the square root at degree k−1
paper.claim: If Mₖ is the Taylor polynomial of M through degree k−1, then [wᵏ](FE) = [wᵏ⁻¹](M²E) = [wᵏ⁻¹]((Mₖ E)Mₖ).

paper.place: The Cauchy–Schwarz bound on the product coefficient
paper.claim: The modulus of [wᵏ⁻¹]((Mₖ E)Mₖ) is at most the product of the Hardy H² norms of Mₖ E and Mₖ.

paper.place: Contraction of the Hardy norm by the weight
paper.claim: For |E| ≤ 1, the H² norm of Mₖ E is at most that of Mₖ. The squared norm of Mₖ is the sum of |bⱼ|² over 0 ≤ j < k, which is at most k.

paper.place: Proposition 7 — the loss from a nonextremal weight at zero
paper.claim: For f in M(p), E holomorphic on 𝔻 with |E| ≤ 1, and n ≥ 1, |[zⁿ](Ef)| ≤ Aₙ(p) − Rqₙ(1−|E(0)|), where qₙ = [zⁿ]q > 0 and R is the slit-disk conformal radius.

paper.place: Pulling f back to the ordinary univalent class
paper.claim: The inverse slit map χ avoids the pole p, fixes zero, and has χ′(0) = R. Thus F = (f∘χ)/R belongs to S.

paper.place: Coefficients of the pulled-back weighted function
paper.claim: For Φ = F · (E∘χ), its coefficients dₖ satisfy |dₖ| ≤ k for every k ≥ 1 and d₁ = E(0).

paper.place: Finite coefficient expansion on the slit disk
paper.claim: On the slit disk Ef = R(Φ∘q). For n ≥ 1, [zⁿ](Ef) equals R times the sum of dₖ [zⁿ]qᵏ over k = 1,…,n.

paper.place: Separating the linear term of the majorant
paper.claim: All coefficients of qᵏ are nonnegative. In the estimate for [zⁿ](Ef), the k = 1 contribution is bounded by R|E(0)|qₙ, and the terms with k ≥ 2 by Rk[zⁿ]qᵏ.

paper.place: The full majorant and its deficit
paper.claim: Summing Rk[zⁿ]qᵏ over k = 1,…,n gives [zⁿ]fₚ = Aₙ(p). Replacing the k = 1 term by R|E(0)|qₙ reduces the sum by Rqₙ(1−|E(0)|).

paper.place: Transfer of the meromorphic germ in Theorem 1
paper.claim: At each n ≥ 1, Lemma 4 applied to the germ of f at zero gives a holomorphic multiplier |E| ≤ 1 with [zⁿ](e · (f∘h)) = [wⁿ](Ef). Proposition 7 bounds this coefficient by Aₙ(p).
paper.declarations: Goodman.IsM.finite_germ_zero Goodman.lemma_four Goodman.composite_slit_deficit Goodman.proposition_seven Goodman.lemma_five Goodman.theorem_one_bound

paper.place: Why unweighted equality forces a rotation
paper.claim: For e ≡ 1, E(0) = h′(0)ⁿ. Equality at any n ≥ 1 forces |h′(0)| = 1 and hence h(z) = λz with |λ| = 1.

paper.place: Effect of a rotation on the coefficient
paper.claim: If h(z) = λz with |λ| = 1 and aₙ = [zⁿ]f, then [zⁿ](f∘h) = λⁿaₙ. Its modulus in degree one equals 1 = A₁(p) for every f in M(p).

paper.place: Saturation of the second coefficient after pullback
paper.claim: If |aₙ| = Aₙ(p) for n ≥ 2, then the normalized slit pullback F satisfies |[w²]F| = 2. The term involving [w²]F in the coefficient sum has strictly positive weight [zⁿ]q².

paper.place: Alignment of the first two Koebe coefficients
paper.claim: For the rotated Koebe function, dₖ = kηᵏ⁻¹. Equality in the coefficient sum forces d₁ = 1 and d₂ = 2η to have the same argument, hence η = 1.
paper.source_words: requires $d_1$ and $d_2$ to have the same argument

paper.place: Recovering the extremal on the whole disk
paper.claim: With η = 1 the pullback gives f = Rq/(1−q)² = fₚ on the slit disk and hence as meromorphic maps throughout 𝔻. Conversely, fₚ attains equality with every rotation h(z) = λz, including the identity.

paper.place: Converse for each unit rotation in the proof of Theorem 1
paper.claim: For e = 1 and n ≥ 2, the reverse implication of Theorem 1 gives equality for fₚ composed with every rotation h(z) = λz with |λ| = 1.

paper.place: Figure 3 — the omitted segment for p = 1/2
paper.claim: For p = 1/2, fₚ maps 𝔻 onto the sphere minus the closed real segment [−2,−2/9]. The line containing that segment passes through fₚ(0) = 0.
paper.source_words: the sphere minus the heavy segment $[-2,-2/9]$

paper.place: Riemann mapping and the preimage of infinity
paper.claim: The planar Riemann mapping theorem gives a disk chart for every proper simply connected plane domain (Rudin, Theorem 14.8). For the spherical target Π a change of coordinate gives a chart φ centered at w₀, rotatable so that φ⁻¹(∞) lies in (0,1).
paper.source_words: after a rotation of $\D$ the point $\phi^{-1}(\infty)$ lies in $(0,1)$

paper.place: Hyperbolic interpretation of the chart pole
paper.claim: In the rotated chart, δ_𝔻(0,φ⁻¹(∞)) = δ_Π(w₀,∞), so φ⁻¹(∞) = tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞) = p.

paper.place: Normalizing the spherical target chart
paper.claim: With a = φ′(0), the function f = (φ−w₀)/a belongs to M(p), and |a| is the target conformal radius R(w₀,Π).

paper.place: Factoring G through a Schwarz function
paper.claim: The map h = φ⁻¹∘G is holomorphic on 𝔻 and fixes zero. At a pole of G the composition is holomorphic in the spherical coordinate at infinity.

paper.place: The derivative as a subordinate coefficient
paper.claim: Near zero, G = w₀ + a(f∘h). For n ≥ 1 this gives G⁽ⁿ⁾(0)/n! = a[zⁿ](f∘h) and hence the bound R(w₀,Π) Aₙ(p) for its modulus.

paper.place: The image forced by geometric equality
paper.claim: Equality at an order n ≥ 2 forces G to be a conformal bijection onto Π = w₀ + a fₚ(𝔻), with f = fₚ and h a rotation in its normalized factorization.

paper.place: The omitted interval of the rational extremal
paper.claim: With B = p+1/p > 2, fₚ = 1/(J−B) maps 𝔻 onto the sphere minus the closed interval [−1/(B−2),−1/(B+2)].
paper.source_words: the complement of $f_p(\D)$ is the segment $[-1/(B-2),-1/(B+2)]$

paper.place: Position of the basepoint relative to the omitted segment
paper.claim: For an extremal target, the omitted segment lies on a line through w₀. Since w₀ belongs to the target, both endpoints lie on one ray from w₀, at distinct distances 0 < ℓ₁ < ℓ₂.
paper.source_words: segment on a line through $w_0\in\Pi$, with endpoints at distances

paper.place: The pole parameter from the endpoint distances
paper.claim: For endpoint distances 0 < ℓ₁ < ℓ₂ from w₀, the model parameter p = (√ℓ₂−√ℓ₁)/(√ℓ₂+√ℓ₁) lies in (0,1).

paper.place: Scale and direction of the extremal target chart
paper.claim: The complex scale a has modulus 4ℓ₁ℓ₂/(ℓ₂−ℓ₁) and direction a/|a| = (w₀−ξ)/ℓ₁, where ξ is the nearer endpoint.

paper.place: Matching the near and far endpoint distances
paper.claim: For B = p+1/p, the scale gives |a|/(B+2) = ℓ₁ at the near endpoint and |a|/(B−2) = ℓ₂ at the far endpoint.

paper.place: The chart onto the prescribed segment complement
paper.claim: The affine map u ↦ w₀+au sends the omitted model interval onto the prescribed segment, matching its endpoints in order of distance from w₀. Thus w₀+a fₚ maps 𝔻 conformally onto Π.

paper.place: Intrinsic parameters of the constructed chart
paper.claim: The chart w₀+a fₚ sends zero to w₀ and p to ∞. Its parameter p equals tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞), and |a| equals the target conformal radius.

paper.place: All centered charts of the extremal target
paper.claim: For the prescribed segment complement, every conformal bijection from 𝔻 onto Π taking zero to w₀ is a disk rotation followed by the chart z ↦ w₀+a fₚ(z) and attains equality at every n ≥ 1.
paper.source_words: composed with a rotation, and attains equality for every $n$

paper.place: Weighted Rogosinski bound for planar targets
paper.claim: For F in S, a Schwarz function h, and holomorphic |E| ≤ 1 on 𝔻, |[zᵏ](E · (F∘h))| ≤ k for every k ≥ 1. This gives the planar endpoint p = 1.

paper.place: Lemma 8 — weighted coefficients in a centered source chart
paper.claim: For meromorphic G from a proper simply connected plane domain Ω into a simply connected spherical target omitting at least two points, let G(z₀) = w₀ be finite. If φ maps 𝔻 conformally onto Ω with φ(0) = z₀ and φ′(0) = Rₛ, then H = (G∘φ−w₀)/Rₜ satisfies |[zᵏ](EH)| ≤ Aₖ(p) for k ≥ 1 and every holomorphic disk weight |E| ≤ 1. The bound includes planar targets at p = 1.

paper.place: Target charts in the planar and meromorphic cases
paper.claim: A centered target chart has the form ψ = w₀+af with |a| = Rₜ. When ∞ belongs to Π the chart can be rotated to put its pole at p, giving f in M(p). For planar Π the normalized f belongs to S.

paper.place: The Schwarz factor between centered charts
paper.claim: For centered source and target charts φ and ψ, h = ψ⁻¹∘G∘φ is a Schwarz function, and H = (a/Rₜ)(f∘h), with |a/Rₜ| = 1.

paper.place: The two bounds for the centered coefficient
paper.claim: For 0 < p < 1 the centered coefficient estimate follows from Theorem 1. At p = 1 the transfer and product estimates of Lemmas 4 and 6 give the bound k for degree k.

paper.place: The disk automorphism centered at z₀
paper.claim: The chart φ(z) = (z₀+z)/(1+conj(z₀)z) has Rₛ = 1−|z₀|² and φ⁻¹(z₀+Rₛ x) = x/(1−conj(z₀)x) near zero. Here conj(z₀) denotes the complex conjugate of z₀.

paper.place: The local change of center in the disk
paper.claim: Near x = 0 the map G satisfies G(z₀+Rₛ x) = w₀ + Rₜ H(x/(1−conj(z₀)x)).

paper.place: Coefficients of the inverse disk chart
paper.claim: For 1 ≤ k ≤ n, the coefficient of xⁿ in (x/(1−conj(z₀)x))ᵏ is binom(n−1,k−1) conj(z₀)ⁿ⁻ᵏ.

paper.place: The disk derivative as a complex binomial sum
paper.claim: The normalized derivative Rₛⁿ G⁽ⁿ⁾(z₀)/(n! Rₜ) equals the sum, for k = 1,…,n, of binom(n−1,k−1) conj(z₀)ⁿ⁻ᵏ [zᵏ]H.

paper.place: The disk bound after the change of center
paper.claim: Lemma 8 with E ≡ 1 bounds the modulus of the normalized nth derivative by Dₙ(p,|z₀|).

paper.place: An extremal at a real disk center
paper.claim: For z₀ = r in [0,1), the target fₚ(𝔻) and map G = fₚ∘φ⁻¹ give Rₜ = 1 and H = fₚ. All terms in the derivative sum are nonnegative, giving equality in every order n ≥ 2, also for p = 1.
paper.declarations: Goodman.diskSharpModel Goodman.diskPhase_real Goodman.extremal_model_data Goodman.coeff_disk_model Goodman.coeff_comp_diskKernel Goodman.coeff_extremal_of_ne_zero Goodman.A_positive Goodman.disk_model_derivativeRatio

paper.place: Sharpness at every complex disk center
paper.claim: For each fixed 0 < p ≤ 1, rotating the extremal from r to any z₀ with |z₀| = r gives a map attaining equality at that center for every n ≥ 2.
paper.declarations: Goodman.diskSharpModel Goodman.star_eq_diskPhase_mul_norm Goodman.norm_diskPhase Goodman.coeff_extremal_scaled Goodman.coeff_comp_diskKernel Goodman.coeff_disk_model

paper.place: Normalizing a convex source chart
paper.claim: For a centered chart φ onto the convex source, s = (φ−z₀)/Rₛ is injective with convex image, s(0) = 0 and s′(0) = 1. It has a holomorphic inverse near zero.

paper.place: The inverse-chart germ on a convex source
paper.claim: Near x = 0, G(z₀+Rₛ x) = w₀ + Rₜ H(s⁻¹(x)), so [xⁿ](H∘s⁻¹) equals Rₛⁿ G⁽ⁿ⁾(z₀)/(n! Rₜ) for n ≥ 1.

paper.place: Lagrange inversion for the normalized derivative
paper.claim: For n ≥ 1, [xⁿ](H∘s⁻¹) = (1/n)[zⁿ⁻¹](H′(z)(z/s(z))ⁿ), with the quotient extended at zero.

paper.place: A bounded factor in the reciprocal convex quotient
paper.claim: The reciprocal z/s(z) lies in |w−1| < 1 and extends with value 1 at zero. It has the form 1+zv(z), where v is holomorphic on 𝔻 with |v| ≤ 1.

paper.place: Binomial expansion of the reciprocal power
paper.claim: The nth power (z/s(z))ⁿ is the sum of binom(n,j) zʲ v(z)ʲ over j = 0,…,n.

paper.place: Degrees contributing after Lagrange inversion
paper.claim: The j = n term contributes zero to degree n−1. For j < n and k = n−j, [zⁿ⁻¹](H′ zʲ vʲ) = [zᵏ⁻¹](H′vʲ).
paper.source_words: the term with $v^n$ does not reach $z^{n-1}$

paper.place: Fourier coefficients of the Fejér kernel
paper.claim: For ζ on the unit circle and k ≥ 1, Kₖ(ζ) is the sum of (1−|j|/k) ζʲ over all integers j with |j| < k.

paper.place: Positivity of the Fejér kernel
paper.claim: For k ≥ 1 the Fejér kernel Kₖ is real and nonnegative at every point of the unit circle.

paper.place: Unit mass of the Fejér kernel
paper.claim: The integral of Kₖ against normalized arc measure on the unit circle equals 1 for every k ≥ 1.

paper.place: Integral representation of the Fejér mean
paper.claim: For z in 𝔻, Ẽ(z) is the integral of E(z conj(ζ)) Kₖ(ζ) over the unit circle with normalized arc measure dσ(ζ).

paper.place: The Fejér mean is an admissible weight
paper.claim: If E is holomorphic on 𝔻 with |E| ≤ 1, its polynomial Fejér mean also satisfies |Ẽ| ≤ 1 throughout 𝔻.

paper.place: The constant term of the centered map
paper.claim: The constant Taylor coefficient η₀ of the centered map H is H(0) = 0.

paper.place: Coefficient convolution with the derivative of H
paper.claim: For k ≥ 1, [zᵏ⁻¹](H′E) equals the sum of m ηₘ εₖ₋ₘ over m = 1,…,k, where ηₘ = [zᵐ]H and εⱼ = [zʲ]E.

paper.place: The Fejér multiplier identity
paper.claim: For k ≥ 1, k[zᵏ](H Ẽ) equals [zᵏ⁻¹](H′E). The Fejér factor on εₖ₋ₘ is m/k, giving the same summands m ηₘ εₖ₋ₘ for 1 ≤ m ≤ k.

paper.place: The weighted derivative coefficient of H
paper.claim: For the centered map H, k ≥ 1, and any holomorphic disk weight |E| ≤ 1, |[zᵏ⁻¹](H′E)| ≤ k Aₖ(p), including p = 1.

paper.place: Powers of the convex-map factor as weights
paper.claim: For 0 ≤ j < n, vʲ is an admissible weight in the derivative estimate of degree k−1 with k = n−j, including the constant weight 1 at j = 0.

paper.place: The binomial factor in the convex-source bound
paper.claim: For k = n−j with 0 ≤ j < n, (k/n) binom(n,j) = binom(n−1,k−1). The sum of the resulting bounds is Dₙ(p,1).

paper.place: The extremal half-plane source
paper.claim: The chart φ(z) = z/(1+z) maps 𝔻 onto Re x < 1/2 and has inverse x/(1−x). At z₀ = 0 the model G = fₚ∘φ⁻¹ maps onto fₚ(𝔻) with Rₛ = Rₜ = 1.
paper.declarations: Goodman.halfPlane_bihol Goodman.halfPlane_inverse_analytic Goodman.halfPlane_inverse_maps Goodman.radius_halfPlane_zero Goodman.extremal_model_data Goodman.convexSharpModel

paper.place: Simultaneous attainment on the half-plane
paper.claim: For each 0 < p ≤ 1, the nth coefficient of x ↦ fₚ(x/(1−x)) is the sum of binom(n−1,k−1) Aₖ(p) over k = 1,…,n. This equals Dₙ(p,1), so the same map attains the convex bound in every order n ≥ 2.

paper.place: Discussion — full coefficient bound and unweighted equality
paper.claim: Theorem 1 gives the weighted bound. For weight one and n ≥ 2 equality requires the extremal fₚ and a rotation, and each rotation gives equality.
paper.source_words: in a stronger form that allows a bounded weight

paper.place: Discussion — two derivative results
paper.claim: Theorem 3 gives both sharp derivative bounds from the stated disk and convex sources.
